items.title: MicroStrategy's Bitcoin Accumulation Milestone
points: Company holdings are within days of breaking its previous all-time record for Bitcoin owned on its balance sheet.
The aggressive buying strategy reflects a corporate treasury management shift, where Bitcoin functions as a reserve asset (a store of value held to meet future obligations, similar to gold reserves).
Institutional-scale Bitcoin purchases by major corporations signal confidence in digital assets as long-term holdings rather than speculative trades.

items.title: Kalshi Volume Fabrication Allegations
points: A researcher published a two-part thread showing a single $5,500 ETH trade accounted for 48-58% of all ETH perpetual futures (leveraged crypto contracts allowing price exposure without full capital outlay) volume on four separate days.
An anonymous source claims Kalshi operates volume incentive arrangements with market makers, creating direct financial rewards for artificial trading activity.
The researcher pre-emptively downloaded and encrypted exchange data to three separate cloud backups to prevent potential deletion of evidence.

items.title: Polymarket's Compliance Breakdown and Fraud Exposure
points: The Wall Street Journal reported fraudsters used stolen debit cards for at least $10 million in theft attempts starting February; payment processor Checkout.com rejected over 80% of deposits as fraudulent versus an industry standard of 1%.

CEO Shayne Coplan told staff to prioritize growth and address regulatory fines later; leadership dropped the same-source withdrawal rule (requiring withdrawals to originate from the same account deposits came from, to curb money laundering) despite employee warnings.
Compliance officer Andrew Clifford resigned in April after flagging fraud; US CEO Justin Hertzberg was fired, though an external investigation concluded Polymarket complied with regulations.

items.title: RawVentures: Staking Rewards as VC Capital Governed by Prediction Markets
points: An ethresear.ch proposal converts a fraction of ETH staking rewards (compensation for validating blockchain transactions, not principal) into a venture capital vault without touching the staked ETH itself.

Investment selection uses prediction markets: vault shareholders forecast specific project milestones before capital deploys, and correct forecasters receive shares from incorrect ones, building an on-chain track record of forecasting accuracy.

The design positions the DAO (decentralized autonomous organization) as an Ethereum-specialist investor; unresolved questions include portfolio pricing, manipulation resistance in prediction markets, and independent outcome verification.

items.title: SEC's Tokenized Stock Exemption Narrower Than Market Assumes
points: The Innovation Exemption only covers two models: issuer-native tokenization (a transfer agent records actual shares onchain) and custodial tokenization (the token carries the same rights, including dividends and voting, as the underlying stock).

Synthetic trackers, derivatives, and equity perpetuals don't qualify; Backpack's BP token is a redeemable claim on an SPV (special purpose vehicle, a legal entity created to hold specific assets) rather than a full shareholder entitlement, so it doesn't yet fit the exemption.
Qualifying infrastructure includes Superstate, Securitize, Figure, DTCC, DinariGlobal, and Ondo.

items.title: Coinbase Opens IPO Allocations for US Retail
points: Coinbase launched IPO allocations for US retail customers through its app, starting with Oura.
This is distinct from the synthetic pre-IPO perpetual futures it offers to non-US users.

items.title: Hyperliquid's HYPE Token Hits All-Time High
points: HYPE token hit a $90.92 all-time high after the platform launched manual borrowing using HYPE and Bitcoin as collateral to borrow stablecoins.
